title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-03-25
content:
Attendees: Liam, Aisha, Diego, Priya, Noah (SRE)
Date: 2026-03-25
Summary:
- Focus this week on kernel selection improvements, KV-cache consistency fixes, and tuning batching heuristics for mixed-sequence workloads.
- Made measurable progress on kernel fallback performance (see perf numbers below).

Kernel work
- Merged PR #1427 which adds a new heuristic for selecting fused attention kernels when sequence_length <= 1024 and batch_size >= 8.
  - Microbenchmarks on p4d show 12-18% CPU/GPU kernel latency reduction for 16k-context window slices.
  - Notes: still seeing regressions on a narrow set of GPT-like layers with rotary embeddings; adding a guard to fallback to baseline kernel if attention scale factor differs by >2%.
- Open issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/issues/978 (rotary-embedding mismatch). Diego to prototype a deterministic check in the loader that flags incompatible kernels at model load time.
- Action items:
  - Diego: prototype runtime guard by EOD 2026-03-27 (SR-621).
  - Aisha: add telemetry for number of fallbacks per model-version (Confluence doc link).

KV-cache
- Fixed a race in async eviction that caused intermittent VA map leaks under heavy prefix-caching load. Root cause: eviction callback not waiting for inflight read ops to complete.
  - Patch is in canary and has prevented the leak in 48h of stress runs.
- Consistency: implemented a quick check that verifies KV version ids at the start/end of a request to avoid stale-cache usage in canary. This check is currently enabled via feature flag kv.strict_version_check.
- Observability: added per-request KV hit/miss tags to traces; sample spans show overall hit-rate ~73% for our demo traffic (up from 61% last week after prefix flattening).
- Action items:
  - Priya: roll the eviction fix to dedicated canary pool on 2026-03-27, monitor mem usage and GC pauses.
  - Noah (SRE): add alert if kv.strict_version_check increases error rate >0.5% over baseline.

Batching
- Tuning experiments with dynamic batching window: tests show that lowering max wait from 10ms -> 6ms reduces p95 latency by ~40ms on interactive workloads, but lowers throughput by ~7%.
- Introduced workload-aware batching policy: route requests with short expected response lengths to a low-latency bucket (small batch size, short wait), and long generative requests to high-throughput bucket.
  - Policy implemented as config: batching.policy.v1 with rules based on model-tags and token-estimate.
- Observed corner-case: when many short requests arrive with heavy KV cache misses, latency increases due to serialization on cache misses. Need to prioritize KV golden-path on low-latency bucket.
- Action items:
  - Liam: land batching.policy.v1 behind feature flag and enable for 10% of hosted traffic on 2026-03-29.
  - Priya & Aisha: add e2e test that simulates mixed seq-length traffic and measures p50/p95/p99 for both buckets.

Metrics / Perf snapshots (canary runs, p4d, 64 concurrent connections)
- Baseline (2026-03-18): mean kernel latency 12.3ms, model step p95 220ms, KV hit-rate 61%.
- Post-kernel-heuristic (canary): mean kernel latency 10.8ms (-12%), model step p95 205ms (-7%), KV hit-rate 62%.
- Post-KV-fix: memory leak no longer reproducible in 48h stress; KV hit-rate ~73% after prefix flattening.
- Dynamic batching trial: low-latency bucket p95 improved by 40ms, throughput -7%.

Risks / Blockers
- Rotary embedding kernel regression (see issue) could cause increased fallbacks and latency spikes for some open models.
- KV eviction fix needs SRE signoff before rolling to Dedicated clusters.
- Batching policy rollout needs careful throttling to avoid throughput cliffs for bulk generation customers.

Meeting notes / decisions
- Agreed to enable kv.strict_version_check only in canary for 2 weeks, then reassess.
- Agreed to ramp batching.policy.v1 to 10% hosted traffic for initial telemetry, keep toggle for quick rollback.
- Kernel fallback guard will be conservative: prefer correct baseline kernel over an experimental fused kernel if mismatch detected.

Misc / notes to self
- Add a short dev doc about how kernel selection scoring works (priority: explain cost model, fallbacks, and how to add new kernel entries). Liam to draft.
- Check-in with model-onboarding about models that use rotary embeddings heavily; get sample artifacts so we can reproduce mismatch locally.

Action items recap (owners and due dates)
- Diego: runtime guard for kernel mismatch (due 2026-03-27).
- Aisha: telemetry for kernel fallbacks & e2e batching tests (due 2026-03-30).
- Priya: roll KV eviction fix to dedicated canary + mem/Garbage collection observation (due 2026-03-27).
- Liam: land batching.policy.v1 behind flag and configure 10% rollout (due 2026-03-29).
- Noah: configure alert for KV strict version check error rate (due 2026-03-28).

Questions for leadership / dependent teams
- Product: is a 7% throughput regression acceptable for a 40ms p95 improvement on interactive flows? Need guidance for default policy.
- SRE: signoff checklist for rolling memory fixes from canary -> dedicated clusters?

Next meeting: weekly sync on 2026-04-01 10:00 PT (standup-style, 30min)

Attachments / references: see linked_artifacts above.
